And when he reflected
that he was repaying such evil injuries,
Mu'nis and his companions,
because they had been accustomed to despising the kings,
and being again fearful for their own lives,
appointed all the gatekeepers of the palace from among their own people.
And they decreed that everyone who entered the court,
whether man or woman,
should be searched,
lest a document enter to the king concerning their affairs.
And they reached such a point,
that even on one of the days when they were bringing in curdled milk for him to eat,
the guards thrust their hands into the pot and searched it.
Then God,
praise to His justice,
cast division and strife between the soldiers and Mu'nis and the rest of the nobles;
and they abandoned them and went out into the desert.
And al-Qahir found an opportunity and killed them all,
and the kingdom was established for him.
And he drove out from the palace all the male singers and female singers;
and he cast out the slaves and the handmaidens bought with money,
and they were sold to merchants without the condition that they were musicians.
Now this al-Qahir, after he put to death many of the leaders and nobles by floggings and seized their property,
then those who remained were dispersed as if upon the edge of the sword.
And they instructed old women and old men from among the Arab scribes,
to relate false dreams to the slaves guarding King al-Qahir,
those who stood above the head of the king by night and by day,
and to the commanders of thousands and hundreds,
saying: "Lo, we see bad dreams concerning you;
rather, beware of the king,
lest he destroy you."
And in this way they also instructed the diviners and astrologers,
so that when they were questioned about this,
they would reply towards that very same purpose.
And when it was confirmed in their minds that al-Qahir was going to destroy them,
on one of the nights, when he had drunk much wine,
they bound him, and blinded both his eyes with hot kohl,
and deprived him of his sight.
These things happened in the year 322,
322 of the Arabs.
This man was seen afterward in the Great Mosque begging for alms,
while another was leading him.
